claims.claim: Describes Draft, Awaiting Decision, FCP accept or reject, and return to Draft.
claims.notes: The current process also states acceptance, rejection, and return-to-Draft branches.

claims.claim: Uses Draft → Awaiting Decision → FCP → Accepted → Implemented → Final.

sources.quote: Once an implemented CAP has been released in a specified version ... it will move to Final.

claims.claim: Treats CAP status, implementation, release, and SCP activation as distinct stages.

sources.quote: When the network time is later than the upgradetime specified in the upgrades command, the validator will vote to update the network

claims.claim: Uses quorum-set/FBA semantics for network activation.

sources.quote: A node’s trusted set of nodes is called a quorum set.
Final when it has been formally accepted by a majority of validators (nodes) on the network.

claims.notes: The consensus documentation uses quorum-set and FBA semantics. The CAP registry still uses global-majority wording for Final.

claims.claim: Treats CAPs, SEPs, and token-holder votes as distinct governance concepts.

sources.quote: agreement is achieved using federated voting

claims.notes: The sources separate ecosystem standards from validator consensus. They provide no token-holder activation vote.

evidenceLines: Live re-check 2026-08-30: https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/core/README.md — the process retained Draft, Awaiting Decision, FCP branches, and return to Draft.
Live re-check 2026-08-30: https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/core/README.md — the workflow continued through Accepted, Implemented, and Final.
Live re-check 2026-08-30: https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/network-upgrades — validators still schedule and vote on network activation after implementation.
Live re-check 2026-08-30: https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/stellar-consensus-protocol — SCP still used quorum sets and federated voting.
Live re-check 2026-08-30: https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/tree/master/ecosystem — SEPs remained ecosystem proposals, distinct from core-protocol CAPs.
siblingSweep: Sibling sweep 2026-08-30: grep Awaiting Decision|Final Comment Period|quorum set|token-holder → q-protocol-cap-process, q-protocol-quorum-slice-vs-quorum, q-protocol-scp-consensus-algorithm, q-protocol-tier1-requirements, q-protocol-validator-upgrade-vote; no contradiction
conflicts: CONFLICT: Uses quorum-set/FBA semantics for network activation. vs https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/core/README.md — Final is still described as acceptance by a majority of validators (nodes), while the consensus guide defines quorum-set/FBA agreement.
overallNotes: The process stages remain supported. The current CAP registry and consensus guide use conflicting activation language.
